2. Criminal Appeal No. 2468 of 2002 arose from the judgment and order dated 22-5-2002 of the Metropolitan Assistant Sessions Judge, 5th Court, Dhaka in Metropolitan Sessions Case No. 711 of 1999 and Criminal Appeal No. 2469 of 2002 arose from the judgment and order dated 22-5-2002 of the, Metropolitan Assistant Sessions Judge, 5th Court, Dhaka in Metropolitan Sessions Case No. 716 of 1999 over the selfsame occurrence, two cases have been registered separately and the prosecution has also examined similar set of witnesses in both the cases. The evidence on one Case would overlap the other and therefore, we would like to discuss the evidence in Metropolitan Sessions Case No. 713 of 1999, in order to avoid repetition. 

 3. Appellants were put on trial to face charges under sections 399/402 of the Penal Code. Some appellants who had faced trial and they pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. Their defence case, in short, is that they have been falsely implicated in the case that they have not assembled at the place of occurrence for preparation to commit dacoity, that they have been arrested from different place and implicated in false case by manufacturing a concocted story and that no arms or other explosives have been recovered from them. 

 4. Md Abu Hena Mostafa Kamal (PW 5) narrated the prosecution case, which is as follows: 

 5. After the case of records were sent before the learned Sessions Judge, the learned Assistant Sessions Judge, who took up the cases for trial, framed charge against the appellants under different counts as mentioned above. Prosecution examined 12 witnesses and tendered 4 witnesses in support of the charges but the defence examined none. The learned Assistant Sessions Judge on consideration of the evidence on record, convicted the appellants under sections 399/402 of the Penal Code and sentenced them to rigorous imprisonment for 10 years with a fine of Taka 5000, in default, to suffer rigorous imprisonment for 6 months more under section 399 of the Penal Code. No separate sentence was awarded to the charge under section 402 of the Penal Code. The learned Assistant Sessions Judge also convicted the appellants and others under sections 332/333/353/34 of the Penal Code and sentenced to rigorous imprisonment for 7 years in lump with a fine of Taka 3000 each, in default, to suffer rigorous imprisonment for 3 months more. 

 6. Mr Md Tareque Morshed, learned Advocate appearing for the appellants, submits that there is delay of about 9 hours in lodging the FIR although the distance between the place of occurrence and the police station is very short and this delay speaks volume that the appellants have been falsely implicated in a concocted case. Learned Advocate further submits that the evidence on record sufficiently supports probability of the defence version that PWs 5 and 14 have been using Doctor Kudarat-e-Khoda hostel of Bangladesh Leather Technology, as their abode for realising money and implicating innocent persons by instituting false cases. Learned Advocate finally submits that the prosecution has failed to prove the charges against the appellants by examining neutral and reliable witnesses of the locality, and that the conviction of the appellants being based upon the evidence of police personnel, the appellants are entitled to get benefit of doubt. 

 7. We have reproduced the testimony of PW 5 while narrating the prosecution case extensively. In cross-examination, this witness stated that there was no alamat in this case, that the seizure lists were not available with the record and that he handed over the medical certificate in support of his injury to the investigating officer, He denied the defence suggestion that he did not sustain any injury or that the appellants were innocent persons and that they were not dacoits. He stated that there was no independent witness of the locality, as the accused persons were not taking preparation on the roof-top of the house of Siddique Mia, a local inhabitant. He denied the defence suggestion that he lodged the FIR as per direction of Monayamul Islam or that Khokan was not arrested from the roof top, or that he had sustained injury when he was taken on the roof top after arrest and that as he had refused to become a witness, he was implicated as an accused in the case. 

 8. Md Sohel (PW 1) is seizure a list witness. He has not supported the prosecution story in terms of the prosecution case about the recovery of arms in his presence from the possession of Khokan. Md Joynal Abedin (PW 2), a Sub-Inspector of police, Md Monwar Hossain (PW 3), another police officer, Md Serajuddullah (PW 4), and Md Younus (PW 6), are formal witnesses. 

 10. Md Idris (PW 8) is a constable. He corroborated the prosecution story in material particulars and stated that he accompanied PW 5 and PW 14 at the time of raiding the house of Siddique Mia, and arresting Khokan and Swapan. He further stated that from their possession arms and ammunition were recovered. He also stated that 3 police personnel including himself had sustained injuries, who were then shifted to Dhaka Medical College Hospital and then to the Bangladesh Medical Hospital and the Rajarbagh Police Hospital. In cross-examination, he stated that he along with Khokan and Abu Hena had sustained injuries with the splinters of the same bomb. He denied the defence suggestion that the appellants were falsely implicated in this case. 

 12. Syed Munaimul Islam (PW 14) is the investigating officer of the case. He stated that he investigated the cases, examined the witnesses under section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, seized alamats by preparing seizure lists and having found prima facie cases against the appellants submitted charge sheets against them. In cross-examination, he stated that he was investigating officer in Sessions Case Nos. 713 and 716 of 1999, that Sub-Inspector Abu Hena Mostafa Kamal was the informant in both the cases, that he did not receive any complaint from the people of Hazaribagh regarding the preparation of commission of dacoity and that they got the secret information about the incident. 

 13. It may be mentioned here that in Sessions Case No. 716 of 1999 the informant has been examined as PW 3, Md Idris (PW 8) has been examined as PW 4, Abu Sayed (PW 7) has been examined as PW 5 and Monaymul Islam (PW 14) has been examined as PW 12. 

 14. We would like to observe that on a total misconception of law the prosecution had instituted two separate cases over the same subject matter, although law authorises a combination of more offences in one trial. Though there is no legal bar of separate trial of the accused for each separate offence but the policy underlying in sections 234 to 239, of which section 239 is relevant for our consideration, is not to cause undue harassment or confusion to the accused persons by giving evidence of a large number of items covering an unduly long period. And that would have also saved Court's valuable time. The simple prosecution case is that acting on a tip off, PWs 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12 and 14 along with other police personnel laid siege to the house of one Siddique Mia of 82 Hazaribagh, apprehended appellants Khokan and Swapan, recovered some arms. ammunition and bombs from their possession, while other appellants fled away by firing and hurling bombs aiming the police force, causing injuries to PWs 5, 8, 11, 14 including Khokan, According to the prosecution, the accused persons were taking preparation to commit dacoity on the businessmen of Hazaribagh. One case has been instituted under sections 399/402 of the Penal Code and the other under sections 332/333/353/34 of the Penal Code. The offences were committed in course of the same transaction. 

 15. Section 233 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (the Code) lays down a general rule that every distinct offence of which any person is accused, there shall be a separate charge and that every such charge shall be tried separately Sections 234,235,236 and 239 are exceptions to this general rule. Since more than one accused person are involved in the cases, section 239(d) is applicable in this case, which reads as follows: 

 16. The object of this exception is to avoid the necessity of the same witnesses giving the same evidence many times over in different trials, and to join in one trial those offences with regard to which the evidence would overlap. This section is an enabling provision and this clause (d) enables a plurality of offence to be dealt with in the same trial. In these cases, the date, the place and the time of occurrence are same. Where more than one person being animated by a common purpose to do certain acts constituting different offences, and there is continuity in their action, shall be regarded as forming one single transaction. As there is continuity of purpose or design, and continuity of action; the acts of the appellants are parts of the "same transaction" within the meaning of the clause. The real requirement is that there must be one continuous thread of a common purpose running through the acts to support a joinder of charge in respect thereof when the accusation against the accused is that they carried out a single scheme by successive acts and there was a complete unity of project and the whole series of acts were so linked together by one motive and design, a joint trial is desirable in order to avoid hardship and embarrassment to the accused. The learned Assistant Judge overlooked this provision of law and unnecessarily wasted Court's valuable time in holding trial of two cases. Similarly, the investigating officer (PW 14) and the public prosecutor failed to point out this defect and wasted their energy twice, which could have been avoided. 

 18. As observed of the above, the appellants Khokan and Swopan were caught red handed from the rooftop of Siddique Mia. The defence plea of Khokan was that he was apprehended from other places and that as he refused to become a witness in the cases, he was implicated as an accused. The positive prosecution case is that Khokan sustained injury on his head with the splinters of bomb. He did not deny the prosecution's claim of sustaining injury on the spot by giving suggestion to the witnesses that he did not to sustain any injury. He gave a lame explanation that when he was taken on the roof-top by the police, he had sustained the injury, which explanation had devoid of substance. In his examination under section 342 of the Code, he did not say that he did sustain injury in the manner he suggested to the witnesses. Though Swapan claimed that he was not in any way involved in the incident, and gave an explanation that as he did not supply water to the police officer, he was falsely implicated in the case. This explanation merits no consideration. 

 20. The private witnesses now-a-days do not come forward to support the prosecution story due to fear of reprisal or other causes. The criminals are using sophisticated arms, which arms are not given to the law enforcing agencies other than the Army. They are using obsolete arms, which are not comparable with those in the hands of criminals. As a result, the method and the rate of crime are increasing enormously. The police are helpless to their tactics and they do not give protection to the witnesses after deposing a case against them as a result, there is tendency of suppressing the real facts by the local witnesses. The public witnesses while discharging public duty unfold a crime and testify on oath about the time, the place and the manner of the incident corroborating each other, and under such juncture, the Court is left with no option but to convict the accused relying upon them, if their testimonies tally each other. These public witnesses have no personal interest to depose against the accused persons other than to disclose the real incident. This is one of such cases, we have to rely upon them. On consideration of the evidence on record, we are satisfied that the prosecution has been able to prove the charge under section 399 of the Penal Code against the accused appellants Khokan and Swapan beyond doubt. 

 22. In this particular case, the appellants Swapan and Khokan along with others not only assembled on the rooftop of Siddique, they had arms in their hands which sufficiently proved the ingredients of section 399 that they were preparing to commit dacoity at that time when they were apprehended by the police. In view of the above, the learned Assistant Sessions Judge was justified in convicting appellants Khokan and Swapan under section 399 of the Penal Code, but he was not justified in finding them guilty under section 402 of the Penal Code. 

 26. Now, let us consider whether the prosecution has been able to prove the charge under sections 332/333/353/34 of the Penal Code. PW 5 stated that he along with his force tactfully reached the roof-top of Siddique Mia's house and apprehended Khokanand Swapan and recovered arm, ammunition and bombs from their possession, and at that time other dacoits hurled 3/4 bombs aiming them at the time of retreat causing injuries to him, Khokan, constable Idris, Sub-Inspector Abul Hossain and Monayemul Islam. He did not disclose who hurled bombs. His statements sufficiently proved that the appellant Khokan and Swapan did not have the opportunity to use criminal force to deter him to discharge his duty, not to speak of causing hurt to the police force. They were apprehended on reaching the rooftop which implied that they were handcuffed and they did not even try to flee away or even attempted to retaliate the police force, rather one of them i.e. Khokan, sustained injury Though PW 8 stated that Swapan hurled a bomb aiming the police force but PWs 5 and 7 did not corroborate him. There is no allegation in the FIR that Swapan hurled any bomb. The positive case is that the other dacoits hurled bombs aiming the police force, which caused injury to PWs 5, 8, 14, Abul Hossain and Khokan. 

 28. Section 353 relates to assault or use of criminal force to deter a public servant while discharging his duties. As observed above, PWs 5, 7 and 8 (PWs 3, 4 and 5 in Sessions Case No. 716 of 1999) failed to prove that the appellants Swopan and Khokan ever caused hurt or used criminal force to these witnesses in discharging public duties. In that view of the matter, the learned Assistant Sessions Judge was wrong in finding them guilty of the charge. As regards the other appellants, as observed above, there is no iota of evidence against them in support of those charges, inasmuch as PWs 5,7,8 did not say that these appellants or anyone of them assaulted or caused hurt or used criminal force at the time of apprehension of Khokan and Swapan. In that view of the matter, we find that there is no legal evidence on record in support of the aforesaid charges. 

 In the result the Criminal Appeal No. 2468 is allowed in part and Criminal Appeal No. 2469 of 2002 is allowed. The conviction of all appellants under section 402/332/333/353/34 of the Penal Code is set aside and they are acquitted of the charge. The conviction of the appellants Swapan and Khokan under section 399 is maintained but they are sentenced to the period they have already undergone in prison. The other appellants except Khokan and Swapan are found not guilty of the charge under section 399 of the Penal Code. The appellants be set at liberty forthwith if not wanted in connection with any other case.
